heroHeadline: Two FDA Oncology Approvals on May 15 — Enhertu Enters Curative-Intent Breast Cancer; First ctDNA-Guided Immunotherapy Approved for Bladder Cancer
heroSubtitle: The FDA approved Enhertu (T-DXd) for early-stage HER2+ breast cancer in both neoadjuvant and adjuvant settings on May 15 — the first antibody-drug conjugate to gain approval in curative-intent early breast cancer, potentially transforming ~30,000 US patients/year. The same day, atezolizumab (Tecentriq) became the first immunotherapy selected by liquid biopsy (ctDNA MRD), approved for ctDNA-positive muscle-invasive bladder cancer after cystectomy — with companion diagnostic Signatera CDx validated simultaneously. ASCO 2026 lifted its embargo on 7,000+ abstracts on May 21, with BREAKWATER, VIKTORIA-1, and EV-302 perioperative bladder data unlocked. The plenary daraxonrasib Phase 3 pancreatic cancer readout is scheduled May 31.
footerNote: Data sourced from FDA Drug Approvals, NIH/NCI, peer-reviewed journals (NEJM, The Lancet, Nature Medicine, JACR), ASCO/ESMO/AACR conference data, and institutional analyses. All clinical data reflect published and presented trial results.
